CFML Language Reference: Functions

DateFormat

Returns the date part of a date/time value as a string, formatted according to a mask. If you leave out the mask, dd-mmm-yy is used.

Category

Display and formatting functions

Syntax

DateFormat(date [, mask ])

Parameters

date
A date/time value or a string that can be converted to one, for example Now() or "12/31/1999".
mask
Characters that describe the format: d day without leading zero, dd with leading zero, ddd abbreviated weekday, dddd full weekday; m, mm, mmm (Jan), mmmm (January); y and yy two-digit year, yyyy four-digit year; gg the era ("AD"). Other characters are copied to the result. You can also pass one of the named formats short (12/31/99), medium (Dec 31, 1999), long (December 31, 1999) or full (Friday, December 31, 1999).

Returns

The formatted date as a string.

Usage

Two-digit year masks are perfectly legal, but this is a Y2K-ready product: please use yyyy. To format the time part, use TimeFormat. LSDateFormat formats dates for the current locale.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Party = CreateDateTime(1999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Mask</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>(none)</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Party)#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>mm/dd/yyyy</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Party, "mm/dd/yyyy")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>dddd, mmmm d, yyyy</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Party, "dddd, mmmm d, yyyy")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>d-mmm-yy</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Party, "d-mmm-yy")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Today</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Now(), "mmm d, yyyy")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
